h: Making a proper Skeggy day of it
p: The aquarium works brilliantly as part of a bigger day at the seaside. It's a manageable size, so a couple of hours will cover the aquarium and Jurassic Falls, leaving plenty of time for the beach, the front and everything else Skegness has to offer. Younger children especially love the treasure-hunting feel, and spotting the different creatures along Long John Silver's trail keeps them engaged from start to finish.

Tips for your visit: try to arrive earlier in the day during the school holidays, when the town gets busy. Ask about feeding times when you arrive, as watching the animals being fed is always a highlight. If you're thinking of the diving or snorkelling experiences, book well ahead and read up on the requirements first.

Once you're back outside, the beach is right there, a huge stretch of golden sand perfect for building castles, paddling and donkey rides when they're about. The clock tower is a great meeting point if your group splits up.

For more animal encounters, Natureland Seal Sanctuary on North Parade has been rescuing and caring for seals for decades, and it's a lovely add-on for little wildlife fans. If you fancy a quieter afternoon, Gibraltar Point National Nature Reserve, just south of the town, has dunes, salt marsh and beach walks packed with birdlife.
Then it's time for the classic Skegness finish: fish and chips on the front, an ice cream and a stroll along the pier as the lights come on. Nobody leaves Skeggy without at least one of those.
